- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates near end of horizon; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment remains neutral or weak.
